pfas.reasoning: 3M's real $10.3B public water system settlement (2023) and DuPont/Chemours/Corteva's real $1.185B settlement are large, negotiated, pre-bankruptcy global settlements covering a broad share of claims -- but no curated PFAS/AFFF defendant has filed Chapter 11 over this liability as of this writing. Real personal-injury claims (15,222 in MDL 2873 as of April 2026) remain in active MDL litigation outside any bankruptcy trust.
pfas.next_stage_watch: Would move to bankruptcy_trust or bankruptcy_preemption if any curated defendant files Chapter 11 specifically over PFAS/AFFF liability -- watch the Material Event (8-K) pipeline for this; none has triggered it as of this writing.

talc.reasoning: J&J is financially solvent, not insolvent -- it has filed Chapter 11 THREE times through two different subsidiaries (LTL Management in 2021 and again in 2023 after the first was dismissed; Red River Talc in 2025) specifically to halt and consolidate MDL 2738 litigation on its own settlement terms, the real pattern academic literature calls 'bankruptcy preemption.' The third attempt was rejected by the bankruptcy court in 2025; J&J announced it will litigate individual cases instead rather than appeal, per real reporting.
talc.next_stage_watch: A fourth bankruptcy attempt, or a return to large individual jury verdicts (the real Ingham pattern -- $4.69B original verdict, reduced to ~$2.1B on appeal) if the bankruptcy route is fully abandoned, are both real possible next moves -- watch the Material Event (8-K) pipeline and JPML's own pending-actions count for signals either way.

turnout_gear.reasoning: MDL-3191 is genuinely new litigation -- JPML's own November 2026 report shows 17 pending actions and 17 total historical (pending equals total, meaning nothing has resolved yet). No curated defendant, no global settlement, and certainly no bankruptcy filing exists for this category as of this writing -- the earliest real stage in the documented progression.
turnout_gear.next_stage_watch: Watch for: a curated defendant being identified (none is yet), the first settlement disclosure in a 10-K/8-K, and the JPML pending-actions count growing past its current 17 -- any of these would be the first real sign of this MDL moving to the next stage.

reserve_development_benchmark.methodology: Real, computed aggregate paid-loss development curves from the Casualty Actuarial Society's public 'Loss Reserving Data Pulled from NAIC Schedule P' dataset (accident years 1998-2007, compiled from real NAIC statutory filings). For each development lag N, the value is the aggregate cumulative paid loss at that lag divided by the aggregate cumulative paid loss at the latest observed lag (10) -- i.e. 'by lag N, this line of business had on average paid out this fraction of what it eventually paid.' NOT PFAS- or talc-specific; these accident years predate that litigation's real scale. Used only as a general products/liability-line benchmark for how slowly claims normally mature -- the same order-of-magnitude-analog role the RAND asbestos DCC ratio plays elsewhere in this project, never an actuarial estimate for any specific curated defendant.
